newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: St George says Advance integration on track.
newsitem.headline: St George says Advance integration on track.

text.p: St George Bank Ltd said on Tuesday its integration of the operations of Advance Bank Ltd was on track following the completion of the regional bank's takeover offer in January.
"The integration process is going well and is ahead of schedule in some area," St George managing director Jim Sweeney said at a media briefing after the company's first half results.
St George earlier said it had revised its estimate of total pre-tax cost saving from the merger to A$175 million within 30 months of the acquisition, up from an earlier estimate of A$140 million.
Sweeney said St George expected to achieve 40 percent of the savings within the first year following the settlement of the acquisition and 80 percent within two years.
The parts of the integration plan which had already been completed, Sweeney said, included the appointment a senior management team and the elimination of the treasury duplication.
"Branch rationalisation has commenced and includes a pilot of various process methodologies with a full program of four closures per week commencing this month," Sweeney said.
Sweeney said the bank expected to close 49 branches by July 1997 and a total of 169 branches over a 30 month period.
Sweeney said the bank had begun the delicate programme of managing customer and staff relations during the branch rationalisation process.
The customer attrition rate after the merger at 2.9 percent was running below the bank's estimated rate of seven percent.
"We are working on a basis of absolute minimal disruption to our customers either through changes to the banking procedures or products and services," he said.
Sweeney said the bank expected to present a single brand to its customers, with the exception of its Bank SA brand in South Australia, by the end of the first quarter of 1998.
"Bank SA enjoys a unique and specific relationship with South Australia. At this stage we are concentrating on shoring up that relationship and protecting it," Sweeney said.
Sweeney ruled out a counter bid for Victorian regional bank, Bank of Melbourne Ltd, currently the target of a A$1.435 billion bid from Westpac Banking Corp.
"St George already has about A$4 billion of assets in Victoria so if the (Westpac/Bank of Melbourne) merger does go ahead we will be competing very strongly down there," he said.
Sweeney said the Victorian market had shown it was prepared to change its allegiances and St George would take advantage of any opportunity to gain market share in that state.
St George earlier posted a half year net profit of A$99.74 million from A$74.52 million a year earlier.
